signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.58, holding above its SMA20 and SMA50 at 157.27 and 157.67 while testing the SMA200 at 158.52. Fed 4.00% (HIKING) vs BoJ 1.25% (HIKING) produces a 275bp policy spread, matched by a +264bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry advantage sustaining the underlying topside drift. However, options skew displays notable asymmetry: 25d risk reversal sits at −1.88 (Saxo, 1M tenor, indicative mid), showing strong downside put demand despite JPY speculative net short positioning of −30,379 contracts (CFTC, week ending Oct 6). ATM IV at 7.7% trades below 30-day realized volatility of 9.8%, creating a negative vol risk premium of −2.1 percentage points that highlights structural complacency in spot despite tail hedging. The 160.00 threshold remains the focal level that has previously triggered Ministry of Finance intervention alerts; intervention risk rises on a sustained break above 160.00. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while spot holds above moving-average support. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct. Risk: Spot rejects 158.52 SMA200 resistance alongside sudden escalation toward 160.00 intervention friction.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short with Vol Hedging Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1178, situated firmly below its descending SMA20 (1.1364), SMA50 (1.1506), and SMA200 (1.1600) cluster. Leveraged funds hold net short −84,775 contracts (CFTC, week ending Oct 6), sitting in the 4th percentile of the 52-week range with a z-score of −1.64, confirming heavily stretched bearish positioning. Fed 4.00% (HIKING) vs ECB 2.65% (HIKING) maintains a 135bp policy rate advantage for the dollar, reinforced by a +143bp SOFR-€STR OIS spread. Meanwhile, EUR/USD ATM IV runs at 6.5% against 4.1% realized volatility, generating an elevated vol risk premium of +2.5 percentage points as institutional participants actively hedge downside extensions. Real rates remain restrictive for the dollar at +1.63% versus +0.30% for the euro, but the BEER valuation model indicates spot is stretched at z = −2.27σ cheap relative to fair value. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, structural policy divergence dominant against crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: ECB meeting 29 Oct — market pricing hold. Risk: Short covering triggers a technical squeeze back above the SMA20 at 1.1364.

signals.title: AUD/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Policy Divergence
signals.text: AUD outperforms all G10 peers across the weekly scorecard with an average gain of +0.413% across 4 pairs, whereas SEK sits as the weakest currency averaging −0.412% across 2 pairs. The resulting leader-to-laggard bilateral spread of 0.825% breaches the thematic alert threshold. RBA policy rate at 4.60% (HIKING) stands 285bp above Riksbank at 1.75% (ON HOLD), establishing a decisive monetary policy and carry wedge. Divergence in macro data momentum reinforces the bilateral gap, with Sweden recording persistent misses at an ESI reading of −17.0 while Australia registers neutral momentum at +1.0. Leveraged positioning shows AUD net long +48,911 contracts, reflecting institutional backing for the currency's high-beta carry profile. Trade bias: Long AUD/SEK, driven by wide yield premium and relative data divergence. Catalyst: RBA meeting 3 Nov. Risk: Spread compresses below 0.80% as global growth concerns undermine commodity-linked high-beta currencies.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Contrarian Divergence vs Macro Bear Flattening
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4266, positioned above its rising moving-average sequence of SMA20 (1.4124), SMA50 (1.3977), and SMA200 (1.3867). Retail sentiment shows an extreme reading of 90% short against 10% long (Retail sentiment data), conflicting directly with CFTC speculative positioning where leveraged funds hold net short CAD of −82,720 contracts (21.2% long). Fed 4.00% (HIKING) vs BoC 2.25% (ON HOLD) yields a 175bp policy rate advantage and a +159bp SOFR-CORRA OIS premium in favor of the dollar. The US yield curve trades in a bear flattener regime with 2s10s at +49.4bp, underpinned by US 5Y yields climbing +24bp over 20 sessions on real-yield expansion (FRED, as of Oct 8). Persistent retail fading into institutional trend accumulation creates elevated short-squeeze risk toward higher multi-month bands. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, supported by rate divergence and contrarian retail skew. Catalyst: BoC meeting 28 Oct. Risk: Spot breaks below the SMA20 support level at 1.4124.
